RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Harper Delgado
Member ID: W927303466
Reference Number: POC-332858B095-32885
Date of Notice: 2026-08-13
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-09
Service: Partial knee replacement (unicompartmental knee arthroplasty), CPT 27446
Treating Surgeon: Dr. Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Blue Cross NC Member Rights and Appeals Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), issued in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-13. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree and ask that this decision be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

Note on plan policy: I requested and reviewed Blue Cross NC's publicly available medical policy materials for this procedure. I was not able to obtain the specific medical-necessity criteria document (medical policy or MCG care guideline) that was applied to my case, and I am not quoting or attributing any specific plan language in this letter because I have not been given that text. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Blue Cross NC provide me and Dr. Reyes with the specific internal rule, guideline, protocol, or clinical criteria (including title, number, and version/effective date) that was relied upon to deny this request, consistent with my right to that information as part of the adverse benefit determination and appeal process. Without that document, I am addressing the stated denial reason using the clinical findings in my chart, in my own words.

1. Imaging findings
On 2026-06-02, MRI of the affected knee showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. This is a severe, isolated-compartment degenerative finding, which is the type of imaging finding that clinicians use to support unicompartmental (partial) rather than total knee replacement. If the denial was based on a belief that the imaging does not show compartment-specific, end-stage disease, that is not consistent with these findings, and I ask that the MRI report and images be re-reviewed.

2. Failed conservative treatment
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-04-08 through 2026-07-01) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note, without resolution of symptoms.
- I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-06, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief.
This represents a sustained, well-documented course of conservative management that did not adequately control my symptoms.

3. Duration and severity of symptoms
I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain that is unrelieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain. On examination, I have positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion that is limited by pain.

4. Absence of contraindications
There is no active infection and no untreated substance use noted in my record. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker. Nothing in my clinical picture indicates a contraindication to surgery.

Taken together, the imaging findings, the 24-month symptom history, the documented failure of physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection, and the functional and exam findings all support that partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) is medically necessary for my condition. I ask that Blue Cross NC reverse the denial and approve this procedure.

Enclosed with this appeal, please find:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-08 to 2026-07-01)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID use; corticosteroid injection 2026-04-06)
- MRI report dated 2026-06-02
- Surgeon Dr. Reyes's clinical notes and exam findings
- [Any additional records the patient/provider wish to include]

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day deadline stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-09). Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing, and please advise me and Dr. Reyes of the specific policy or guideline criteria used in the original determination, as requested above, as soon as possible so that we may respond fully if any additional information is needed.

If you have any questions or need additional information, please contact me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address]. You may also contact my surgeon's office, Dr. Reyes, at [Provider Office Phone Number], for any clinical clarification.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Harper Delgado
